messages:

Cc: procurement@novapro.com

Subject: New vendor stuck on login — POs on hold

Hi Marissa / Ben,

We're in the middle of onboarding two vendor entities (NovaPro Components & NovaPro Logistics) and users report they get a 401 / 'session expired' error immediately after they complete the supplier form. The Coupa account shows the vendor as "Submitted" but our finance team can't see the pending POs; they're stuck in approval.

Screenshots attached (login-error-401.png). Can you confirm whether this is on our side or something in the Redwood supplier gateway?

Urgent: two POs are scheduled for Tuesday morning and procurement asked to pause payments until this is fixed.

Thanks,
Sylvia Patel

NovaPro Supply

Subject: Re: New vendor stuck on login — POs on hold

Sylvia,

Thanks for the quick report and the screenshot — very helpful. I dug into the Coupa sync logs and the vendor records appear to have completed the form step, but our access gateway is returning a short-lived session token that is being rejected by the Coupa callback (401). That explains the "Submitted" state (record created) but no PO visibility (Coupa's callback failed to mark vendor as active).

I've CC'd Ben and Karthik — Ben for escalation to the gateway ops team, Karthik for SSO/session behavior and whether any recent cookie TTL changes rolled out this week.

Short ask: can we get a log extract from the gateway around 2026-12-30T23:00Z (attached: log-snippet-20261230.txt) and confirm whether a config push happened between 22:45–23:15Z last night? Procurement needs an ETA; if this can be hotfixed we'll unblock the POs.

Marissa

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: New vendor stuck on login — POs on hold

Marissa / team — attaching quick notes from ops after an initial look.

Summary: at ~23:00Z on 12/30 there was a short config artifact in the gateway rollout that changed session cookie max-age from 14 days to 15 minutes for a subset of tenant bindings (a rollout flag meant for internal canaries mistakenly included tenant pattern matching). That resulted in the callback from Coupa attempting to validate a signed JWT that had just expired. The token expiry mismatch leads Coupa to treat the callback as failed even though form submission finished.

Impact: affected tenant patterns: novapro-*.coupa.com (two vendor entities). Visible effects: 401 on final redirect, vendor stuck in Submitted, PO not visible to finance.

Workaround deployed: rollback of the config flag at 18:00 PST; ops confirmed gateway now issues the 14-day cookie again, but clients whose browser or integration attempted to authenticate during the window may need a fresh redirect to acquire a valid token.

Next steps: 1) We recommend NovaPro end-users clear their session and try the vendor review flow again; 2) We'll re-run the Coupa callback replay for the two vendor records to force the 'activate' transition; 3) schedule a quick canary test at 01:30Z to validate.

Jonas — can you coordinate the replay with NovaPro or do you want Procurement to accept a manual activation while we run the replay?

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
